meta_title: Troubleshooting VpnHood! SERVER: Port Already in Use | VpnHood!
meta_description: Fix the problems VpnHood! SERVER most often runs into, such as another program already using its port, on a managed or a standalone server.
title: Troubleshooting
lead: What to do when VpnHood! SERVER runs but something keeps it from working, on a managed or a standalone server.
inuse_see: The server runs, but apps cannot connect. Its log, [server_log], shows [log_address_in_use] for its port, and [manager_err_no_tcp] when it could open none of its ports. A managed server shows the same error in VpnHood! MANAGER: see A server shows an error.
inuse_why: Another program on the machine already uses the server's port, [server_port] unless you changed it. Most often it is a web server such as nginx or Apache, another VPN or proxy, or a second copy of VpnHood! SERVER.
inuse_find: To find it, run this on the server, with your port if it is not [server_port]:
inuse_name: In what it prints, the program's name follows [ss_users]: [ss_users_example] is nginx.
fix_stop: Stop the other program if you don't need it. For a service such as nginx, this also keeps it from starting at boot:
fix_port: Move the server to another port, as in Set your server's IP addresses, or for a managed server in MANAGER, as in Change an address. Keys you have already given out carry the old port: see Keys you have already given out.
fix_copy: If the program is VpnHoodServer, another copy of the server runs, such as one installed on Linux and one in Docker. Keep one, and uninstall the other: see Uninstall on Linux or in Docker.
inuse_restart: Then restart the server with [server_restart_linux], or with [docker_restart] in Docker, so it opens its port again.
